\[
T = m\, \frac{100 - t}{100},
\quad
I_{\text{out}} = \begin{cases} 255 & I > T \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases},
\qquad s = 15,\ t = 15
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(m\): The mean of the s by s window
- \(s\): The window size
- \(t\): The percent below the mean at which pixels turn black

m is the mean of the s by s window around the pixel. A pixel turns black when it is at least t percent darker than m, and white otherwise. Bradley and Roth sum each window with an integral image, so the cost per pixel does not depend on s. PixelNexus uses running sums, which give the same sums. Their method improves on Wellner's, which compares each pixel with a moving average of the last s pixels of the scan. They cite Wellner's choices of s as one eighth of the image width and t = 15. Since T is a fixed fraction of the mean, making the whole image darker or brighter by a factor gives the same result. The result is 255 where the value is above the threshold and 0 elsewhere, or the reverse with Invert.
